name: Formation of Dense Partonic Matter in Relativistic Nucleus-Nucleus Collisions at RHIC: Experimental Evaluation by the PHENIX Collaboration
notes: PHENIX white paper evaluating the first three years of RHIC data, recorded with the collaboration's own title wording and result_type 'measurement' (not 'discovery').

significance.locator: arXiv:nucl-ex/0410003, abstract (no single significance/sigma value stated)
significance.note: A collaboration-wide assessment paper, not a single-significance result. Recorded as a measurement, not as a discovery or observation.

summary.plain: In 2005 the PHENIX collaboration published its own review of the first three years of RHIC data on collisions of atomic nuclei. It concluded that the state of matter created cannot be described in terms of ordinary colour-neutral hadrons.
summary.technical: PHENIX's white paper (Nucl. Phys. A 757, 184-283) evaluates the measurements from the first three years of RHIC operation (charged-particle multiplicities, transverse energy, identified-hadron yields and spectra, elliptic flow, two-particle correlations, fluctuations and high-pT suppression) with an emphasis on implications for the formation of a new state of dense matter, and finds that the state of matter created cannot be described in terms of ordinary color neutral hadrons.

title: Formation of Dense Partonic Matter in Relativistic Nucleus-Nucleus Collisions at RHIC: Experimental Evaluation by the PHENIX Collaboration
why_it_matters: The abstract says the results are examined with an emphasis on implications for the formation of a new state of dense matter; the paper's title calls this dense partonic matter.
